exposure: Indomethacin and cefazolin (I/C) use during and following exam-indicated cerclage (EIC)
cohort: The study included singleton pregnancies undergoing exam-indicated cerclage (EIC) for painless cervical dilation between 16 and 23 weeks' gestation with dilation ≥1 cm, at a single center between 2013 and 2022.
finding: The use of indomethacin and cefazolin (I/C) at the time of exam-indicated cerclage (EIC) was not associated with increased latency to delivery but was associated with lower rates of intra-amniotic infection.
birth_weight: Median birth weight was a secondary outcome measured at delivery.
gest_age: Exam-indicated cerclage (EIC) was performed between 16 and 23 weeks' gestation; gestational age at delivery was a secondary outcome.
